title: Verruca vulgaris (HPV wart): epidermal hyperplasia + cytoplasmic vacuolization
vignette: A 17-year-old boy comes to the office due to a facial lesion. The patient noticed a small area of rough skin on his lower lip several weeks ago, which has progressively enlarged. He reports no pain or itching. The patient had eczema during early childhood but has had no other chronic medical conditions. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination findings are shown in the exhibit, which reveals hyperkeratosis, acanthosis (thickened epidermis), and papillomatosis (enlargement of the dermal papillae). There are no other skin rashes, oral lesions, or enlarged lymph nodes. Which of the following histopathological findings are most likely present in this patient's skin lesion?

clues.text: small area of rough skin on his lower lip
clues.note: A rough, progressively enlarging skin-colored papule is the classic presentation of a common cutaneous wart (verruca vulgaris).
Warts are typically asymptomatic (non-tender, non-pruritic), which helps distinguish them from inflammatory or blistering lesions.
Hyperkeratosis + acanthosis + papillomatosis is the histologic signature of an HPV-induced wart; koilocytic (vacuolated) cells accompany it.

whatMatters: A rough, painless, enlarging papule with hyperkeratosis, acanthosis, and papillomatosis = verruca vulgaris (common wart) caused by human papillomavirus. HPV histology shows EPIDERMAL HYPERPLASIA (acanthosis) with perinuclear CYTOPLASMIC VACUOLIZATION (koilocytosis). Answer B.
strategy: Recognize the HPV wart and recall its microscopic hallmark: epidermal hyperplasia plus koilocytes (cells with perinuclear cytoplasmic vacuolization). Reject acantholysis + multinucleated giant cells (herpes), subcorneal neutrophils/bacteria (impetigo), and subepidermal linear immune deposits with separation (bullous pemphigoid).

options.text: Acantholysis and multinucleated giant epithelial cells
Subcorneal bacterial collection and neutrophilic infiltration
Subepidermal linear complement deposits and separation

eliminations.label: Acantholysis + multinucleated giant cells - herpes simplex
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: intraepidermal acantholysis with multinucleated giant epithelial cells (Tzanck) = herpes simplex (HSV) infection. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: HSV causes painful, recurrent vesicles/ulcers, not a rough painless wart, and shows giant cells rather than koilocytes. ✅ Correct if: grouped painful vesicles with a positive Tzanck smear.

eliminations.label: Subcorneal neutrophils/bacteria - impetigo
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: subcorneal collection of neutrophils with gram-positive bacteria = impetigo. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: impetigo presents with honey-colored crusts and neutrophilic infiltrate, not a hyperkeratotic verrucous papule. ✅ Correct if: superficial pustules/honey crust in a child.

eliminations.label: Subepidermal linear deposits + separation - bullous pemphigoid
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: subepidermal split with linear IgG/C3 deposits along the basement membrane = bullous pemphigoid (anti-hemidesmosome). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is a tense-bullous autoimmune disease of the elderly, not a wart. ✅ Correct if: tense bullae with linear basement-membrane immunofluorescence.

reasoning: Rough, painless, enlarging papule with hyperkeratosis/acanthosis/papillomatosis = verruca vulgaris (HPV wart)
HPV drives keratinocyte proliferation (epidermal hyperplasia) and koilocytic change
-> epidermal hyperplasia + cytoplasmic vacuolization; answer B
mechanism: Cutaneous warts (verruca vulgaris) are caused by human papillomavirus (HPV), a non-enveloped double-stranded DNA virus that infects basal keratinocytes and drives their proliferation. Histology shows epidermal hyperplasia (acanthosis), overlying hyperkeratosis, papillomatosis (upward projection of dermal papillae), and characteristic KOILOCYTES - keratinocytes with a perinuclear cytoplasmic clearing/vacuolization and raisinoid nuclei, the cytopathic effect of HPV. The same koilocytic change is seen in HPV lesions elsewhere (e.g., condyloma acuminatum, cervical dysplasia). Warts are usually diagnosed clinically and are self-limited but can be treated with salicylic acid, cryotherapy, or immunotherapy. The distractors correspond to other dermatologic entities: HSV (acantholysis + multinucleated giant cells), impetigo (subcorneal neutrophils/bacteria), and bullous pemphigoid (subepidermal split with linear basement-membrane immune deposits).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Micro/Derm > HPV: verruca vulgaris/condyloma; histology = epidermal hyperplasia, hyperkeratosis, papillomatosis, koilocytes (perinuclear vacuolization).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Identify the wart clinically, then match it to koilocytic/epidermal-hyperplasia histology.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on koilocyte, acanthosis, papillomatosis, hyperkeratosis, or acantholysis? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Acantholysis + giant cells = HSV; subcorneal neutrophils = impetigo; subepidermal linear deposits = bullous pemphigoid.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: On the histology exhibit: thickened epidermis (acanthosis), heaped keratin (hyperkeratosis), and upward dermal papillae (papillomatosis). Anchor: 'verrucous surface + koilocytes = HPV wart.'

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: HPV wart -> epidermal hyperplasia + koilocytic vacuolization; same koilocytes in cervical HPV.

memoryHook: HPV puffs up the epidermis and hollows out the cells - koilocytes with a halo - turning skin into a rough, painless wart.
